title: slot-lease hedger and fallback router for Dedicated fleet
author: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Dedicated fleet clients can see hard failures when slot leases evict unexpectedly during transient cluster pressure (scale-down, preemption, or spot churn). These failures disproportionately impact low-latency SLAs because callers are routed to a slot that immediately becomes unavailable. Context: We've historically relied on short-lived leases + immediate eviction propagation; that model reduces tail capacity but doesn't hedge for short window churn. This PR introduces a two-part approach: 1) a Slot Lease Hedger that maintains a small local safety pool by renewing a fraction of expiring leases proactively and amortizing renew attempts across the cluster; 2) a Fallback Router that routes in-flight requests away from slots with elevated churn risk and ensures an in-request fallback path to a compatible warm slot (same model/quantization family). Goals: reduce hard-failure rate during transient churn by >60% while keeping reserved capacity waste under 3% of active pool. Changes in this PR: - runtime: slot lease hedger (pkg/fleet/lease/hedger.go) with jittered renew windows, exponential backoff, and per-tenant soft caps. - router: fallback route selection in internal/allocator/router.go that augments the routing score with a volatility penalty derived from lease-failure rates and recent heartbeats. - control plane: metrics and tracer hooks for hedger decisions (deploy/charts/dedicated/values.yaml and docs/operational/slot-lease-hedging.md). - e2e: deterministic failure simulator to reproduce preemption windows and verify fallback behavior (e2e/tests/slot_failover_test.go). - docs: operator guide, rollout checklist, and an opt-out runtime flag for tenants. Design notes: - Hedger selects up to N hedges per node where N = max(1, ceil(0.02 * node_slots)) but respects tenant soft caps. Hedging is cooperative: nodes advertise hedges to avoid duplicated renews. - Fallback routing uses a volatility score aggregated by the control plane with 1m and 5m windows; slots with volatility > threshold are penalized. - Fallback path prioritizes warm slots with recent KV cache affinity to reduce cold-token overhead. Tests and validation: - unit tests for hedger state machine and backoff logic. - integration tests for routing scoring with synthetic volatility signals. - e2e failure replay demonstrating a 68% reduction in hard-failures and 1.9% extra slot utilization in a 2000-slot cluster (results embedded below). Rollout plan: 1) feature gated off by default; enable as opt-in for a small set of Dedicated customers; 2) monitor metrics (hard_fail_rate, hedger_success, fallback_latency) for 72h; 3) progressively enable cluster-wide with a 1%-10%-50% ramping policy. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] e2e failure-replay - [x] docs and operator runbook - [x] feature flag + telemetry - [x] post-merge canary rollout knobs

release_notes: Introduce Slot Lease Hedger and Fallback Router for Dedicated fleets. Reduces hard-failure rate during slot churn with minimal extra slot utilization. Configurable via helm: hedger.enabled, hedger.max_fraction, router.volatility_window_ms, router.volatility_penalty_cap. Opt-in controlled; recommended gradual rollout.
operational_results: Canary run results (2000-slot cluster, 48h): baseline hard_fail_rate=0.0125 -> hedger+fallback=0.0039 (68% reduction). Average extra slot utilization=1.9% (within target <3%). Median fallback_latency=6ms, p99 fallback_latency=38ms. Observed hedger_success=98.6% and hedger_redundant_renewals=0.6% (advertise cooperation effective).
